focus: Adaptive Hierarchical Depth Selection via Capability Composition
question: Will a prospectively deployed adaptive depth‑selection policy, derived offline by selecting the depth that minimized observed error for each horizon, achieve higher expected utility (i.e., lower average planning error) than any single fixed‑depth policy on a held‑out set of planning tasks?
hypothesis: When evaluated on a held‑out set of planning tasks, the adaptive policy will produce a statistically lower average planning error than the best static depth policy identified from the same observational data, yielding a positive G_A (approximated as the difference in expected utility between the two interventions).
next_action: Execute the described provider_probe experiment on HuggingFace, collect the evidence, and then perform a focused FZG analysis to quantify G_A and update the adaptive policy if needed.
